title: Edgecase Decision Storyboard & Sample Bank
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, personal storyboard and sample bank for handling small-but-frequent edge cases that keep tripping up annotators and downstream models. Intended as a working cribsheet for annotators + first-pass adjudicators, not final policy. Use for quick training, pair-adjudication sessions, and to seed unit tests for the evaluation harness.

High-level goals (why this doc exists):
- Capture narrative-style examples (short stories) that show where label ambiguity arises in context.
- Provide suggested quick-decisions for annotators to keep throughput high when confident, plus clear escalation triggers for adjudication.
- Offer sample text snippets to include in unit tests / evaluation prompt sets.
- Log unresolved tradeoffs and questions for the formal guide.

Quick decision flow (1-line):
- If you can resolve with a single deterministic rule (token-level, regex, or canonicalization) -> label and add a small comment.
- If resolution requires factual inference beyond the text or knowledge about user intent -> tag for adjudication and add a short note on the inference made.
- If multiple labelers disagree or the case materially affects downstream scoring -> escalate to peer-review + include sample in the "clarify-and-block" set.

Quick flags to use in comments: (short codes for speed)
- QC-RULE: deterministic regex/canon applied
- QC-INFER: we made an inference beyond explicit text
- QC-MULTI: multiple plausible spans/labels exist
- QC-PROMPT: candidate would change model output quality if mis-labeled

Confidence tags for fast triage (recommendation):
- CONF-3: high confidence (rule-based, consistent examples seen >10x)
- CONF-2: medium (some ambiguity but consistent with local context)
- CONF-1: low (requires knowledge outside text or author intent)

Storyboard frames (annotator POV). Keep short, repeatable.

Frame A — 'Identifier-ish numbers'
- Example: "Order # 00421-89 was processed."
- Issue: Are hyphenated alphanumeric tokens labeled as PRODUCT_ID or left unlabeled?
- Quick-decision: If the token appears in a dedicated id slot (Order / Invoice / Tracking) -> label as ID.PRODUCT; mark QC-RULE; use CONF-3.
- Adjudicator note: if same token appears elsewhere as natural language (eg part of SKU in free text) then re-evaluate for PRODUCT vs ID overlap.

Frame B — 'Quoted bot messages inside transcripts'
- Example: Agent: "Please click the link: https://safe.check/abc" User: "I clicked it, nothing happened"
- Issue: Should the URL inside the agent quote be labeled as LINK if it's inside a quoted message? Some pipelines strip quoted content.
- Quick-decision: Label URL occurrences regardless of quoting as LINK; add QC-PROMPT if quoting indicates system-generated text. CONF-2.

Frame C — 'Abbreviations that look like names'
- Example: "Spoke with Dr. J yesterday"
- Issue: Does J get labeled as PERSON? Abbrev without punctuation?
- Quick-decision: If single-letter followed by punctuation or title prefix (Dr., Mr., Prof.) -> PERSON. If single-letter standing alone and ambiguous -> abstain and mark QC-MULTI. CONF-2.

Frame D — 'Temporal fuzzy spans'
- Example: "We saw it last winter, maybe Dec or Jan"
- Issue: label as DATE with normalized value?
- Quick-decision: label full span as DATE but use free-text normalization field to capture ambiguity ("Dec/Jan, winter") and tag QC-INFER. CONF-1.

Concrete sample bank (ready-to-copy examples):
1) "Tx ref: 00-FF-07A arrived." --> expect: ID.TRANSACTION: "00-FF-07A" (QC-RULE, CONF-3)
2) "Customer: J. Miller called in." --> expect: PERSON: "J. Miller" (QC-RULE if punctuation present)
3) "System: "Your passphrase is abc123"" --> PASSCODE? We currently mark as SENSITIVE and redact. (QC-PROMPT, CONF-2)
4) "I met them at the cafe — we said 'see you in the AM'" --> AM ambiguous -> DATE/TIME label: span="AM" with normalization="morning (ambiguous)" (CONF-1)

Annotation micro-rules (speed-first heuristics):
- Prefer token-level deterministic rules for common id-like patterns (dates, invoice refs, hex ids, GUID-like strings). Add a comment reference to the regex used.
- Titles (Mr/Ms/Dr) attached to single uppercase initial -> label as PERSON if punctuation present.
- If a candidate span is a URL and it contains embedded identifiers (e.g. /order/1234) capture both: LABEL:LINK span=url, SUBSPAN:ID.ORDER - if UI can't support nested tags, prefer labeling as LINK and add comment with the sub-id.

Sample adjudicator script (pair session):
1) Two annotators label a batch of 50 borderline examples (from the sample bank).
2) Adjudicator collects QC codes and confidence tags.
3) For each QC-INFER or CONF-1 case, annotators write 1-sentence rationale.
4) Adjudicator decides, records canonical rule (if any), and adds a unit-test snippet to the eval repo.

Sampling heuristics to expand the bank:
- Pull 200 random samples where model confidence dropped >0.2 and human labels disagreed.
- Stratify by token type (id-like, date-like, url-like, short-initials, quoted) to avoid overfitting to one type.
- Keep a rolling "top 20" list of newly observed patterns; rotate into pair-adjudication weekly.

Open questions (to convert into formal policy later):
- How do we treat single-letter initials when co-referenced with full names elsewhere in a doc? (partial co-ref resolution needed).
- Do we agree on a single canonical normalization format for fuzzy dates across datasets? (e.g., "winter 2023" vs "Dec 2023/Jan 2024")
- Should quoted system text be considered part of the user utterance for labeling purposes? (upstream pipeline variance).

To-do (personal):
- Extract 50 examples from the recent adjudication queue and seed unit tests. (blocking: access to eval repo).
- Draft regex snippets for common id patterns and add to shared snippet library.
- Run a 1-hour pairing session (Noah + Marisol) and log divergences.

Small notes to self (observations from labeling last month):
- Annotators tend to under-label hyphenated alphanumeric ids when they appear mid-sentence; seems like UI selection friction.
- When adding comments, short codes (QC-*) are actually getting used; standardize codes in a single Confluence page.
- Adjudicators prefer paired rationale rather than long monologues — keep prompts to 1 sentence.

If you use any of these snippets for the formal guide, add a link back here so I can prune the bank later.

-- Marisol
(last edited: quick triage after afternoon session)
